messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] about the configuration result
messages.subject_clean: [irace-package] about the configuration result
messages.body_plain:
Dear Zhenxi,

There are many reasons why this can happen:

* Does the parameter actually have an effect on the algorithm? If not, irace is
basically selecting one value at random and the chosen elite will be random.

* What is the variance of the algorithm across multiple runs? irace does not
magically reduce this variance (nothing will). If the variance is large enough,
some runs will be luckier than others, so irace may converge to different
elites and also the gap computed in few runs will be misleading.

* How much budget was given to irace? Some users expect to be able to run irace
with few hundred evaluations or even less just because there is one training
instance and one parameter with very few values. But this is not the scenario
for which irace was designed. In such a scenario, it is always better to do a
full factorial or fractional experimental design and no racing or a single
race, as mentioned in the user-guide. Irace is designed for the case where your
parameter space is large enough that it makes sense to do a search within it
and your budget is large enough that it makes sense to run several races.

There are many other reasons why the above may happen. Without some more
details about your set-up (scenario.txt, parameters.txt, target-runner, how do
you measure the gap, etc), it is impossible for anyone to tell.

Best wishes,

Manuel.

messages.subject: [IRACE-Tuning budget] Is there any way to force IRACE using all the training instances even though the tuning budget is low?
messages.subject_clean: [IRACE-Tuning budget] Is there any way to force IRACE using all the training instances even though the tuning budget is low?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

My case: I have 36 training instances and a budget of 300 experiments. I run IRACE and only 12 instances were used (one third of the total amount).

Is there any way to force IRACE using all the training instances even though the tuning budget is low for the amout of provided training instances or should I increase the budget value?

Best wishes,

André

messages.subject: Re: [IRACE-Tuning budget] Is there any way to force IRACE using all the training instances even though the tuning budget is low?
messages.subject_clean: [IRACE-Tuning budget] Is there any way to force IRACE using all the training instances even though the tuning budget is low?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Andre,

You can force irace to evaluate more instances by adjusting the setting of irace.
This should be done with caution especially because you have a very small budget.
So I add small explanation here so you can decide:

First, if you can increase the budget I would advise you to always do it. A good budget value
will depend mostly on the number of parameters you have to configure, irace needs evaluations to
explore and exploit the parameter space, the bigger the space, the more evaluations are likely to be needed.
Now, increasing the budget will not necessarily increase the number of instances, most probably
it will, but not much.

If you force irace to evaluate more instances, irace distributes the budget to increase the precision of the
performance evaluation and thus, you reduce the number of configurations of your algorithm that irace can test. Normally we advice
to force more instances to be evaluated  when the instances are heterogeneous. This means that is not easy to find a
good configurations for all the instances, so irace needs to focus on evaluate many of them to know what is really good.
On the other hand, if your instances are homogeneous, meaning that best configurations are good for all the instances,
then is ok to evaluate few instances.

If you are using the last irace version I recommend you to adjust the elitistNewInstances setting (by default 1).
irace will add elitistNewInstances new instances each iteration to the evaluation list.

Complementary, you can adjust the settings related with the elimination tests: firstTest (default 5) and eachTest (default 1).
The firstTest option will set the number instances required to apply the first statistical test to eliminate bad
configurations and eachTest will set the intervals of how many instances are required to apply the elimination
test after firstTest.

I hope this can help you let me know if you have more questions.

Bests,
Leslie.

messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] Re: [IRACE-Test instances] Is it possible to run the testing automatically just after the ending of IRACE tuning in training instances?
messages.subject_clean: [irace-package] Re: [IRACE-Test instances] Is it possible to run the testing automatically just after the ending of IRACE tuning in training instances?
messages.body_plain:
It seems you (or your irace.bat) are calling the R function irace() directly, instead of using irace.main() or irace.cmdline(), like the wrappers we provide do. The function irace() does not do testing, however, the higher-level wrappers irace.main() and irace.cmdline() do.

For example, in inst/bin/irace.bat:

@echo off
:: Windows has problems with spaces in directory names. Thus, it is better to
:: install R somewhere like "C:\R". You also need to add both R and the
:: directory where irace.bat is located to the PATH.
:: To edit the PATH in Windows, search for "Environment variables" in the
:: control panel, then edit PATH, then
:: add a string similar to "C:\R_PATH\bin;C:\IRACE_HOME\bin", where R_PATH
:: should be R's installation path and IRACE_HOME is irace's installation path
:: (the output given by running 'system.file(package="irace")' within R).
R.exe --vanilla --slave -e "library(irace);irace.cmdline()" --args %*

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.body_plain:
(Reposting here without the data in case it is useful for someone else)

Hi Andreas,

The seed should not affect too much the results. It is just a variance reduction technique.

I plotted the frequency that the parameters are sampled using parameterFrequency() and the algorithms seem to be sampled almost equally with a small advantage for ILS, However, looking at the parameter space, it seems that once the ILS is chosen, the other parameters are mostly disabled, so there is not much diversity there.

Looking at the avg rank per algorithm type, it seems ILS is often the best (probably conditional to the parameters found by irace). See boxplot.

Looking at the restarts, they are happening every iteration, so irace is already trying to increase diversity by sampling. At least for now, irace does not have any niching mechanism to enforce diversity, it only increases diversity by sampling more widely, but if the new solutions are worse, they will get eliminated and lose diversity again.

The R code I used for my analysis is attached.

This is an interesting benchmark because the parameter space is very unbalanced. It would be even more interesting if you can find a better non-ILS configuration without prior knowledge in the same amount of experiments (consistently in independent runs since irace could also find that configuration by chance). It would clearly show something that should be improved in irace.

If you want to do a test, I would suggest to do additional runs of irace. Adding more budget (longer runs of irace) is not going to help because it seems too easy to get trapped in good ILS configurations.

Thanks,

Manuel.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Andreas,

--batchmode only works if irace can run in the submission node and query the computing nodes for the status of jobs. You need to know the type of job scheduler and write a target-runner that submits jobs to the submission node. It is quite cumbersome to be honest. I'll be very happy to accept contributions if someone decided to improve it or move to something more advanced like: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/BatchJobs/index.html

--parallel without --batchmode should work almost everywhere. What you are seeing is a bug in Windows that will be fixed in irace 3.0. If you don't mind using a development version of irace, we can provide it to you.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Manuel,

I took a look at the sources.

I think any cluster system could be more easily supported and readily out of the box if one could define three applications:
submit.exe - submits a job and returns the ID
stat.exe - checks whether the job ID is terminated
fetch.exe - fetches the job's results and outputs the cost (or fails if the job failed)

Currently, submit.exe can already be defined as target.runner and fetch.exe can be defined as target.evaluator.
However stat.exe cannot be parameterized because it's fixed to "qstat" and several out of the box supported cluster systems (SGE, TORQUE, etc.).

If you would add a "cluster.stat" parameter (pointing to an executable or script) in addition to "target.runner" and "target.evaluator" the out of the box supported cluster systems could become a configuration option and would not need to be hard-coded. In addition anybody can could use irace together with his or her cluster system. I assume there was a reason why qstat was hard-coded though.

Is there something else I am missing?

Sincerely,
Andreas

messages.subject: Re: (single) Instance file generation and usage - MATLAB.
messages.subject_clean: (single) Instance file generation and usage - MATLAB.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bali,

If you mean that you have a benchmark function in your code that takes different instance parameters, you can create a trainInstancesFile (instances.txt) file like:

myfunction n=2 d=10
myfunction n=2 d=20
myfunction n=2 d=30
myfunction n=3 d=30

Then irace will pass something like "myfunction n=2 d=10" to target-runner and target-runner needs to pass that to your matlab code.

MATLAB is tricky to configure because it cannot be made executable, like other programming languages, and it is hard to pass parameters to it and run it as a stand-alone program. The example we distribute with irace used to work some time ago. It seems every new version of Matlab becomes worse at this!

If you know R, there is a matlabr package that may help. Then, you can write targetRunner as an R function that directly interfaces with matlab code.

Otherwise, you have to figure out how to pass parameters to your matlab code from target-runner in some other way. One possible approach could be to write in target-runner a file containing all the info that you need (instance, parameters values, seed) and make your matlab code read that file and set the variables. There are other ways you can find around:

https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/answers/97204-how-can-i-pass-input-parameters-when-running-matlab-in-batch-mode-in-windows

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3335505/how-can-i-pass-command-line-arguments-to-a-standalone-matlab-executable-running

But I don't know which methods work with recent versions of Matlab and we don't have matlab to test it.I know people have made it work in the past, but they didn't share how with me (the only example is the one already distributed with irace)

If you get it working, I'll be happy to add it as an example to irace. The more general you make it, the better. Please let us know!

Cheers,

Manuel.
